name: MonarchFileTypeIcon
title: FileTypeIcon
wrapsNative: MonarchIcon (SF Symbols) chosen from the file name, the MIME type or a UTType
summary: A glyph for the family of a file (image, PDF, spreadsheet, archive and so on), worked out from its name and MIME type, with a spoken name.
whenToUse: Beside a file name in a list, an attachment chip or an upload row, and as the large mark of a file that has no preview.
whenNotToUse: When a real thumbnail of the file exists, show the thumbnail. For a general symbol that is not a file type, use MonarchIcon.
api: MonarchFileTypeIcon.init(_ family: MonarchFileTypeFamily, size: MonarchFileTypeIconSize = .md, label: String? = nil, isDecorative: Bool = false)
MonarchFileTypeIcon.init(fileName: String?, contentType: String? = nil, size: MonarchFileTypeIconSize = .md, label: String? = nil, isDecorative: Bool = false)
enum MonarchFileTypeFamily: String { case image, video, audio, pdf, document, spreadsheet, presentation, archive, code, text, other }
enum MonarchFileTypeIconSize { case sm, md, lg }

options.name: family
options.description: The family to draw, when it is already known.

options.name: fileName
options.description: The file name or path; its extension decides the family when the MIME type does not.

options.name: contentType
options.description: The MIME type. A specific type takes precedence over the extension.

options.name: size
options.description: sm is a 16-point glyph, md 20 points, lg a 24-point glyph on a 40-point tile.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of the family.

options.name: isDecorative
options.description: Hides the icon from assistive technology when nearby text already says the type.

states.name: decorative
states.description: The icon is hidden from VoiceOver; nothing changes visually.

appearance: Each family has its own SF Symbol, tinted from the data palette (images and video data 1, documents and text data 2, spreadsheets and code data 3, audio and presentations data 4, PDF data 5) or the muted text colour for archives and other files. The large size sits on a muted tile with a subtle border and 8-point corners. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web and Android draw one page outline with a mark inside; iOS uses a distinct SF Symbol per family, which is what the Files app does. The extension and MIME tables are the web's, so a file gets the same family on every platform; a type the tables do not list is looked up with UTType, and MonarchFileTypeFamily(_: UTType) accepts a UTType directly, which the web cannot. The large size is a 24-point glyph on a 40-point tile (the web draws 28 on 40). The web's FileTypeGlyph is not a separate type: pass isDecorative.
accessibility: The icon is one image element whose label is the family name, for example "PDF document", from the component's strings table or the label parameter.
With isDecorative the icon is hidden from VoiceOver.
Every family has a different symbol, so the type does not depend on the tint.
The glyph and the tile scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A name with no extension, a leading-dot name such as .env and an unknown extension give the other family.
application/octet-stream and an empty MIME type are ignored and the extension decides.
A double extension uses the last part: backup.tar.gz is an archive.
The icon is not interactive and has no touch target of its own.

parityExceptions.reason: The web draws its own file glyphs; iOS draws the SF Symbol for each file family in the same colour per family and the same order, so the glyph shapes differ.
